summary: The study describes the atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ultrafine MoS2 nanocrystals on a porous cobalt foam current collector using molybdenum hexacarbonyl and hydrogen sulfide as precursors. The resulting Co@MoS2 electrode demonstrates excellent electrocatalytic performance for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), with a low overpotential and high stability, making it a promising candidate for efficient and durable anodes in water electrolyzers.
evidence: Ultrafine molybdenum sulfide (MoS2) nanocrystals are grown on a porous cobalt (Co) foam current collector by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using molybdenum hexacarbonyl and hydrogen sulfide as precursors. The Co@MoS2 electrode exhibits a low overpotential of only 270 mV to attain an anodic current density of 10 mA cm-2 and shows excellent long-term stability.
